tool.name: otx_lookup
tool.description:
Look up an IoC in AlienVault OTX (Open Threat Exchange). Third 🟡 important item from the §10 expert-pentester gap audit. Different signal from VirusTotal (#71): OTX gives **attribution context** (which threat actor / campaign / TTP) rather than **multi-engine consensus** (how many AV vendors flagged it).
OTX is AT&T's free community threat-intel platform — security researchers publish "pulses" (curated indicator lists tied to specific actors / campaigns / TTPs). When an IoC appears in multiple OTX pulses, it's been attributed to specific threat actors by independent analysts.
Auto-detected IoC types:
| IoC type | Detected by | OTX endpoint type | |---|---|---| | IPv4 / IPv6 | parses as `ipaddress` (private/loopback/link-local rejected) | `IPv4` / `IPv6` | | domain | apex/subdomain regex | `domain` | | file-md5 / file-sha1 / file-sha256 | hex string of 32/40/64 chars | `file` | | url | starts with `http://` / `https://` (URL-encoded for endpoint) | `url` | | cve | `CVE-YYYY-NNNN` | `cve` |
Severity tuning (based on `pulse_info.count`): - **High** (CWE-453, malicious_target) — `pulse_count >= 3` (multi-analyst attribution). - **Medium** (CWE-453) — `pulse_count` 1-2. - *(no finding)* — no pulses reference the IoC.
Each finding lists the top 5 pulses (name, author, modified date, description excerpt, tags, TLP, industries, targeted_countries) so the agent / user can investigate the attribution context.
Auth: `STRIX_OTX_KEY` env var (free at otx.alienvault.com). Without it, returns `success=False` with a clear error so the agent falls back to other reputation sources (`vt_reputation` #71 / `domain_reputation` #63).
OTX 404 response = "no data on this IoC" treated as success with `no_data=True`, NOT failure.
Cache: per-(ioc_type, ioc_value) JSON cache under `~/.strix/otx_cache/`, 6-hour TTL. Stale-cache served on network failure (fail-open with `error` populated). Cache hit re-emits findings from cached data. Disable with `STRIX_OTX_NO_CACHE=1`.
Each finding carries severity-tailored `description_plain` + `recommended_action` (high → review pulses for attribution, cross-reference IoCs from same pulses with scan findings, perimeter-block; medium → review pulse for attribution, treat as medium-priority signal). `verification_status=needs_review` since pulse data is community-authored.
MITRE technique: T1596 (Search Open Technical Databases) — surfaced via #66 ATT&CK tagging.
Composes with cluster-A safety: rate-limit applies; `--exclude-path` doesn't apply (URL is otx.alienvault.com, not the customer's domain).
Pairs naturally with `vt_reputation` (#71) — VT for consensus signal, OTX for attribution / campaign context.

parameter.name: ioc
parameter.description: Indicator value. Auto-detected as IP / domain / hash (md5/sha1/sha256) / URL / CVE. Private/loopback/link-local IPs rejected.

returns.description:
{success, ioc, ioc_type, otx_url, queried_at, from_cache, pulse_count, severity, pulses: [{id, name, author, modified, created, tags, description, tlp, industries, targeted_countries}, ...], general: {indicator, type, country_code, asn, ...}, findings_emitted, error?, no_data?}.
The agent should: 1. Pair OTX results with `vt_reputation` (#71) for a complete reputation picture (VT = consensus, OTX = attribution). 2. Cross-reference high-severity OTX hits — if a pulse ties an IoC to a known APT group / campaign, the scan posture should reflect that threat-model context. 3. Investigate top pulses' tags and `targeted_countries` / `industries` to understand whether the customer's scan target is on the actor's known targeting list.
